title: Korean Couples Count Their Love in Days

slides.headline: Korean couples count their love **in days, not years.**
slides.note: Day 100, day 200, day 1,000. Each one gets its own celebration.

slides.headline: Day 100 is **the first big one**
slides.body: Flowers, a nice dinner, often matching rings. For many couples, 100 days is the first anniversary that really counts.

slides.headline: The idea **came from babies**
slides.body: Baegil (백일) marks a baby's 100th day, from a time when surviving it was worth a feast. Couples borrowed the milestone.

slides.headline: The first date **counts as day 1**
slides.body: So day 100 lands 99 days after you got together. Couple apps keep the count on the home screen.

slides.headline: Couple days **on the 14th**
slides.body: Valentine's, White Day, Rose Day, Kiss Day. By popular count, nearly every month has one on the 14th.

slides.headline: Being a couple **is something you show**
slides.body: Matching rings, matching outfits, a shared profile photo. The milestones give everyone a date to show it on.

slides.headline: You count years. **Koreans count days.**
slides.body: Many couples abroad wait for the one-year mark. In Korea, you'd hit day 100, 200 and 300 before then.

slides.headline: Singles **get a day too**
slides.body: On April 14, Black Day, single people eat jjajangmyeon (짜장면), black bean noodles. Half joke, half ritual.

slides.headline: In Korea, **love comes with a counter**
slides.body: Every day together adds one. Every hundred gets a party.

slides.headline: Korea, explained **by a Korean.**
slides.body: Follow for the context behind the things Korea does.

caption:
Korean couples don't wait a year for their first anniversary. They celebrate day 100, then day 200, then day 300.

The count starts on the day you get together, the idea comes from a baby's 100th-day feast, and there's a couple day on the 14th of nearly every month. Singles even get Black Day.

What milestones do couples celebrate where you live?
reply: Some couples don't even wait for day 100. Day 22 has a name too: tutu (투투), from "two-two," and it's a small excuse for a date or a gift. Then comes Pepero Day on November 11, when couples trade chocolate sticks. What's the first milestone couples actually celebrate in your country?
fact_check: 4장 '사귄 첫날을 1일로 센다': 가장 널리 쓰는 방식이고 커플 앱 대부분의 기본값. 사귄 다음 날을 1일로 세는 커플도 있음.
5장 '12': 매월 14일 기념일(다이어리·밸런타인·화이트·블랙·로즈·키스·실버·그린·포토·와인·무비·허그데이)은 비공식 대중 문화. 'By popular count'로 한정함.
3장 백일 유래: 영아 사망률이 높던 시절 100일을 넘긴 것을 축하한 풍습이라는 설명이 일반적.
8장 블랙데이(4월 14일) 짜장면: 널리 알려진 관습이나 실제로 챙기는 사람 비율은 소수. 'Half joke'로 톤 조절.
댓글 투투(22일)·빼빼로데이(11월 11일): 비공식 기념일. 빼빼로는 상표라 댓글에서 'Pepero Day' 명칭만 사용.
